title: docs(adr): ADR-0067 D2 says atomicity is a SQL-driver guarantee and "production is SQL", but remote Turso is SQL and cannot roll back
body:
domain:server#6 · huangyiirene · session_01J8VVAnTcb4cZVkPdhkPicW

Filing gate: ① documentation defect with a named producer. The ADR's own sentence reads against the code on `main`, and #32396's defect came from that premise.
reach: named producer. `docs/adr/0067-commit-history-and-rollback-for-ai-authoring.md` line 79 (D2's *Driver caveat*: "in-memory drivers have no real transaction; atomicity is a SQL-driver guarantee. Production is SQL") and line 128 (consequences: "Turn-atomicity is a **SQL-driver** guarantee; in-memory loses it"). `driver-turso` extends `SqlDriver`, yet on the remote arm it declares `supports.transactionsUnsupported` (`turso-driver.ts`, `transactionsUnsupported: this.transportMode === 'remote'`; rationale at `remote-transport.ts`, #18616 / #18063). Per ADR-0119 D1, the engine then runs a `transaction()` callback with no transaction and no rollback. So "production is SQL ⇒ atomic" does not hold for a remote-Turso production deployment.

## Ruling (maintainer)

- **Who / words / where:** the maintainer (account owner `huangyiirene`), verbatim 「同意」, in session `session_01J8VVAnTcb4cZVkPdhkPicW` on 2026-11-12. It answered the seat's three options for this caveat (A amend the ADR / B note it in driver-turso docs only / C make remote Turso transactional), where the seat recommended A. **Ruled: A.**
- C (real transactions on the remote transport) was not ruled. It is separate product work and needs its own card if wanted.

## Expected (option A)

Amend ADR-0067, as a dated Amendment entry in the ADR's own style, with no rewrite of the historical decision text:

1. D2's caveat: atomicity holds only where the engine can roll back (`engineCanRollBack(engine)`, i.e. the default driver really begins, commits and rolls back). Name the drivers that cannot: in-memory, remote-arm Turso, OData (`transactionsUnsupported: true`). On those, package publish takes #32396's path (PR #32454): judge every draft before any write, then undo by compensation on a mid-promotion failure, naming any undo that fails. That is best effort, not atomic: a crash between promotion and undo can still half-land.
2. Line 128's consequence: the same scope, worded the same way.
3. Cite ADR-0119 D1 (the no-rollback degrade) and #32396 / PR #32454.

`docs/adr/**` is a governed surface (Tier H), so it needs an approval from `GOVERNED_APPROVERS`. It is a prose-only change: no code, no contract face.

## Business reason

Who: anyone who reads ADR-0067 to judge whether AI authoring on a remote-Turso deployment can half-land. Today the ADR tells them it cannot. #32396 shipped exactly that half-land.

## Reader

The `domain:server` seat that claims it after triage (with `Ruling-ref:` to this card's body ruling).

## Duplicate check

Written from the seat's #32396 review (lane ACCEPT on PR #32454, "Out of scope" row). No separate search beyond the open `domain:server` queue read at clock-out.
